standard.title: First Nations media and identity
standard.description: investigate the ways First Nations Australian media artists and/or producers celebrate and challenge multiple perspectives of Australian identity through media arts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore how First Nations Australians use media arts to continue and revitalise cultures, and how cultural expressions change over time. They have not yet investigated specifically how First Nations Australian media artists celebrate and challenge multiple perspectives of Australian identity — or analysed how media arts provide a voice through media institutions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate how First Nations Australian media artists and/or producers celebrate and challenge multiple perspectives of Australian identity through media arts, evaluating implications for community debate and audience relationships.

nodes.label: First Nations media arts and Australian identity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how First Nations Australian media artists and/or producers explore and challenge concepts and histories of Australian identity — identifying specific media arts strategies used.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate one First Nations Australian media artist or producer's work and explain at least two specific ways they use media arts to explore or challenge a concept or history of Australian identity.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate how First Nations Australian media artists explore and challenge concepts and histories of Australian identity; examine how media arts provide a voice through film, television and online platforms; use Viewpoints questions to analyse ideological stance; investigate specific works and practitioners (music videos, feature films, CSAs, advertisements, news reports).
wider: Compare two First Nations Australian media artists or producers who explore Australian identity through different forms (e.g. feature film and social media) — examining how each uses their form to communicate different aspects of lived experience or identity, and evaluating what each form can and cannot communicate

Investigate how First Nations Australian media arts depict issues such as The Stolen Generations, land rights, racism, family or dispossession — examining the specific media arts strategies used and evaluating the potential impact on broader community understanding
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding how specific First Nations Australian media artists use media arts to address Australian identity is the foundation for evaluation of community debate impact — without it, subsequent analysis of celebration and challenge has no specific evidence base.

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints questions to examine ideological stance: 'What ideology or philosophical stance is taken in this work?', 'What audience relationships does it seek to create?', 'What multiple ways of understanding does it communicate?'

success_criteria: Student can identify at least two specific ways a First Nations Australian media artist uses media arts to explore or challenge Australian identity
Student can connect the media arts strategies used to the specific aspects of Australian identity being addressed

nodes.label: Celebrating and challenging — multiple perspectives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare and critique multiple First Nations Australian media artists' use of their practice to celebrate and challenge perspectives about Australian identity — evaluating implications for community debate and audience relationships.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare how two First Nations Australian media artists celebrate or challenge Australian identity — identifying at least one shared and one different strategy, and evaluating how each might affect community understanding.
nodes.typical_width: Compare and critique multiple practitioners; analyse how media arts provide a voice for First Nations Australians through institutions and media forms; evaluate potential impact on audiences and community debate; investigate how First Nations Australians use media arts to highlight care for Country/Place and challenge community debate.
wider: Compare and critique the work of three or more First Nations Australian media artists or producers — examining how each uses their practice to communicate multiple ways of understanding an issue, and evaluating which approaches are most effective at creating productive community debate

Investigate how First Nations Australian media arts representations of Australian identity have changed across different platforms and periods — analysing what forces (institutional, technological, social) have enabled or constrained the range of perspectives expressed

response_modes.reason: Vary the practitioners, platforms and issues investigated — multiple artists, multiple forms, multiple issues — to ensure students develop a genuinely diverse understanding of First Nations Australian media arts practice, not a single representative example.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of First Nations Australian media artists, platforms, issues and historical periods available for comparative investigation at Y9-10 is genuinely rich — students who investigate across multiple practitioners and contexts develop much more accurate and sophisticated understanding.
success_criteria: Student can compare at least two First Nations Australian media artists' approaches to celebrating or challenging Australian identity
Student can evaluate how each approach might affect community debate or audience understanding
